clue.text: Shortly, Samuel will welcome Sidney back for painful practice

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the shortened name holds the other piece
shortly means the name Samuel is cut down to its familiar short form

parts.note: the full name Samuel

indicators.note: back means the name Sidney's short form is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sid is the usual short form of Sidney

explanation.surface: Sam is about to have Sid round, and something unpleasant is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses Sid's name and 'will welcome' puts it inside the shortened Samuel. 'Painful practice' could suggest a dentist, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is the practice of taking pleasure in inflicting pain on others.

clue.text: Bird present in plant by lake

indicators.note: in places the word for the present moment within the word for planting

parts.note: to plant seed is to sow it
present in the sense of the current moment, now
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted in some vegetation beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun in the scene, but it is the verb SOW, which 'in' opens to take NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white Arctic bird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Took out someone a bit past it

definitions.meaning: to take someone out romantically is to date them
something a bit past it is old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Went on a date with someone who is getting on a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated is both the past tense of dating someone and an adjective for something outmoded.

clue.text: Soccer war stirred up by one not moving in field

indicators.note: stirred up suggests the letters of soccer war are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Trouble at a football match is provoked by a player who stays rooted to the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One not moving in field' reads like a static footballer, but the field is a farmer's.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a stationary figure standing in a crop field to frighten birds away.

clue.text: Family standard husband abandoned when moving

parts.note: kin means one's family

indicators.note: abandoned means the husband is dropped from the moral standard

parts.note: an ethic is a moral standard
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A family's principles, deserted by the husband when they relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' removes H from ETHIC to leave ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic describes motion; kinetic energy is the energy of a moving body.

clue.text: King seen, perhaps, giving party

parts.note: K is king, and in a down clue NEES UP tells you to write NEES upwards, which gives seen; perhaps flags the indirect route

explanation.surface: A monarch is spotted, perhaps, throwing a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse device: NEES UP, read as an instruction in a down entry, means writing NEES upwards, which spells 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A knees-up is British slang for a lively, boisterous party with dancing.

clue.text: Girl from the middle of Panama becoming saint

indicators.note: the middle of applies to each of the three words that follow, taking their central letters

explanation.surface: A young woman from Central America is being made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle of Panama' suggests geography, but it covers all three words: NA, OM and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Mad Hatter is taking on top end counsellor

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters are scrambled, playing on Alice's Mad Hatter
the end of the word top is its final letter

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's Mad Hatter is seeing a therapist at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' is a single character in the surface; 'Mad' is the anagram signal for HATTERIS plus P, the end of 'top'.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist offers counselling, so a counsellor is a near-synonym for one.

clue.text: Rough reportedly served on ship

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is being heard rather than read

parts.note: crude means rough or unrefined

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone did a tough stint at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be crewed is to have been worked as crew aboard a vessel.

clue.text: He could kill staff supporting strike

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece below supports the piece above it

parts.note: to strike is to hit
to man something is to staff it

explanation.surface: Workers backing an industrial strike, and one of them looks dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'strike' look like industrial relations; 'supporting' puts MAN beneath HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a hired assassin, so he is someone who could kill.

clue.text: Boycott a cost rise that's outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wild and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Consumers urge a boycott of a price increase they find scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to shun or exclude, as a boycott shuns a person or business.

clue.text: Enormous honour presented by Home Counties

parts.note: the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE) of England

explanation.surface: A huge British honour handed out by the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means extremely overweight, so it is a near-synonym for enormous in size.

clue.text: Boiled rice occasionally described as golden?

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, here every other one, are taken

explanation.surface: Boiled rice sometimes comes out a golden colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'golden oldie', a much-loved old song; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hit song is commonly called a golden oldie, so an oldie is something described as golden.

clue.text: Worried after reports of large scale credit crunch

indicators.note: after places the worried piece behind the heard piece
reports of signals that a phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: large scale is mass and credit is tick, as in buying on tick, giving mass tick
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Anxious after news of a huge credit crunch in the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit crunch' is a financial phrase in the surface; it splits, with 'crunch' the definition. Tick is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew food, which is what you do when you crunch it.

clue.text: Equipment army used to imprison resistance

indicators.note: imprisoning something means holding it inside, so the army encloses the resistance

parts.note: a legion is a Roman army unit, or any large army
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Kit an army used to lock up members of a resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a shackle, a piece of restraining equipment for a prisoner.

clue.text: German chap was electrocuted — about time!

indicators.note: about means the electrocution phrase goes round the time piece

parts.note: got fried is slang for being electrocuted

explanation.surface: A German man was finally given an electric shock, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation; 'about' is the insertion signal for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottfried is a German male first name, as in the philosopher Gottfried Leibniz.

clue.text: I'm on licence in various places

indicators.note: on in an across clue places I'm after the licence piece

parts.note: a pass is a licence or permit
taken as written, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone out on licence is turning up all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On licence' suggests parole; it is a placement signal followed by PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin used in references to mean that something occurs throughout a text, at many points.

clue.text: Keep going, having disposed of energy guzzling appliance

parts.note: having sold something means having disposed of it

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so the appliance takes in the energy

parts.note: an iron is a household appliance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Carry on regardless, after getting rid of a power-hungry machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy guzzling appliance' reads as one phrase; 'guzzling' puts E inside IRON to give IERON.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for persevering through difficulty, carrying on.

clue.text: Drunk wife straddled horse? On the contrary

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride something, so one piece goes round the other
on the contrary reverses the roles: the horse goes round the wife, not the other way

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: An intoxicated wife sat astride a horse, or was it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: As written, the wife straddles the horse; 'On the contrary' swaps it so STEED holds W.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is British slang for drunk, alongside sozzled and pickled.

clue.text: Fabrications found by Welsh chap in the papers

parts.note: Dai is a common Welsh man's name, short for David
fabrications are lies

explanation.surface: Made-up stories about a Welshman turn up in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: The dailies are newspapers published every day, so they are the papers.

clue.text: Lecturer has staple treatment applied for the inexperienced

indicators.note: treatment suggests the word staple is worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An academic gets a basic course applied for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the red L signs that British learner drivers must display on their car.
explanation.definitionFit: L-plates mark a car driven by a learner, so they are for the inexperienced.

clue.text: Caption giving information in form of light

indicators.note: in form of places the information within the light

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a kind of light
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A caption explaining things by means of a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In form of' is the insertion signal. Gen is British slang for information, and LED stands for light-emitting diode.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the caption under a picture or the key to a map.

clue.text: Tough but very much present!

parts.note: so, as in 'so kind', means very much
to be present is to be there

explanation.surface: Hard luck, but I'm definitely here!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough!' is a defiant retort, and so is the answer; the rest builds it word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are defiant exclamations meaning 'too bad for you', said to end an argument.

clue.text: Secure land abandoned by thousands — how sad!

indicators.note: abandoned by means the thousands leave, each word losing one

parts.note: to book a seat is to secure it
to land a fish is to hook it
K stands for thousand, and two of them are thousands

explanation.surface: Property deserted by thousands of people: what a shame!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned by' removes a K from each of BOOK and HOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo-hoo imitates loud crying, used as an exclamation of mock sorrow.

clue.text: Children showing high energy

parts.note: meat that is high has gone off
spring means bounce or energy

explanation.surface: Kids displaying boundless energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High energy' looks like one phrase; 'high' is OFF, as of food going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children, their descendants.

clue.text: Large quiet pile with desirable parking

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a lump is a pile or heap

explanation.surface: A big, peaceful country house with a coveted parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two routes: P plus LUMP, and also PLUM ('desirable') plus P ('parking').
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means rounded and fleshy, so it is a near-synonym of large.

clue.text: Contribution to out-take is reversed!

indicators.note: is reversed here asks for opposites of each half, not letters read backwards

parts.note: in is the opposite of out and put of take, so each half of the answer swapped for its opposite gives out-take

explanation.surface: A contribution to a film's discarded footage gets turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' here means swapping each half of out-take for its opposite, not reading the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An input is a contribution someone makes, such as ideas to a discussion.

clue.text: Godfather may be facing extinction

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A Mafia godfather could be on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godfather' is one word in the surface but must be split in two: the Greek god and an informal father.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is the emblem of endangered species, long threatened with extinction.

clue.text: First of haunting autumnal images Keats used to write poem

indicators.note: first of applies to each of the following words in turn, taking their opening letters

explanation.surface: Keats evoked haunting autumn images in his verse, like his ode To Autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese form of poem with three lines.

clue.text: Sign for dance heads removed, showing lack of insight

indicators.note: heads are the first letters, and each of the three words loses its own

explanation.surface: Making a gesture for dance moves betrays a lack of understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads removed' drops S, F and D from the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge or understanding, the opposite of insight.

clue.text: Complex fellow takes fish back into work

indicators.note: into means the reversed fish goes inside the word for a work

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work

indicators.note: back means the fish's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An awkward man brings fish back to his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the fish and 'into' places it within the work. 'Complex' is the noun of Freud's Oedipus complex, not an adjective meaning difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus gives his name to the Oedipus complex, so he is the man behind a complex.

clue.text: Consumption makes a comeback during week at Nice

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run in reverse
during means the letters sit within the words week at Nice

explanation.surface: Tuberculosis returns in the course of a week on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' poses as the old name for tuberculosis; 'during' and 'makes a comeback' take EKATNI from 'week at Nice' and turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Intake is the amount of food or drink consumed, so it means consumption.
